text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices drifted lower — US crude closed around $89.62 per barrel, down from recent highs — after the stock had risen sharply over the prior three trading days (climbing from $135.59 to $142.28). The modest daily decline follows that run-up and may partly reflect profit-taking, though the price remains near recent peaks.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly Iran's escalating threats as a third U.S. carrier arrived in the Persian Gulf, would normally support energy prices by raising supply-disruption risk. However, broader economic signals—including caution from retailers on holiday inventory and shipping cost pressures—may be tempering expectations for near-term oil demand, keeping a lid on prices despite the headline risk.
